title: Which pairs of primes up to 100 have the same two digits?
description: The digits of each two digit prime are swapped, and the new number is looked up in the list of primes. The pairs that survive are written down.
teaching_notes: One idea: swap the digits of a two digit prime and keep the pair only when the new number is also a prime. Watch for students who stop at an odd-looking number such as ninety one and call it prime.

video_script.why: The child swaps the digits of each two digit prime from the sieve list and checks the new number against the same list.
video_script.substitution: Swap the two digits of a prime and look the new number up in the list of primes.
video_script.anchor: The two digit primes on cards, with a swap arrow that turns each card around
video_script.payoff_line: The pairs are seventeen and seventy one, thirty seven and seventy three, and seventy nine and ninety seven.

final_answer.spoken: three more pairs share their digits

maths_rules: 17 swapped is 71, a prime; 37 swapped is 73, a prime; 79 swapped is 97, a prime
11 swapped is 11, so no new pair; 13 and 31 are the pair already given
swaps 23 to 32, 29 to 92, 41 to 14, 43 to 34, 47 to 74, 61 to 16, 67 to 76, 83 to 38, 89 to 98 are even; swaps 53 to 35 and 59 to 95 are multiples of 5
video_script.design: Each prime card is flipped to swap its digits; the flipped card stays teal when it is on the list and is crossed out in amber when it is not.

narration: <bookmark mark='nineteen'/>Step two, check the other swaps. Nineteen becomes ninety one, which is seven times thirteen, so it is not prime.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Twenty three becomes thirty two, which is even. Fifty three becomes thirty five, a multiple of five.
